- SSL certificate của DMS endpoint được quản lý ngay trong DMS, không phải thông qua AWS Network Firewall

67.text:
CORE CONCEPT
RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections for high-concurrency Lambda invocations, preventing "too many connections" errors.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Lambda-to-RDS "too many connections" at peak load — Lambda can scale to many concurrent executions, each opening a new DB connection, exhausting the connection limit
- the fix must address connection exhaustion specifically, not Lambda compute or API Gateway throughput

CORRECT ANSWER: B — RDS Proxy between Lambda and the RDS instance
- Maintains a warm, pooled set of database connections that Lambda functions share and reuse
- Decouples the number of concurrent Lambda invocations from the number of actual DB connections opened
- Purpose-built by AWS specifically to solve this Lambda-to-RDS connection-scaling problem

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Increasing Lambda's concurrency limit allows even more simultaneous connection attempts, worsening the problem
- C — API Gateway's rate limit controls incoming API request rate, unrelated to database connection exhaustion
- D — More Lambda memory speeds up function execution but does nothing to reduce the number of concurrent DB connections opened

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- "Too many connections" + Lambda + RDS almost always points to RDS Proxy
- Distinguish compute-scaling knobs (concurrency limit, memory, API rate limit) from connection-pooling solutions — only the latter fixes DB connection exhaustion

RDS Proxy pool và tái sử dụng kết nối database cho các lần gọi Lambda với concurrency cao, ngăn lỗi "too many connections".

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- lỗi "too many connections" giữa Lambda và RDS khi tải peak — Lambda có thể scale lên nhiều execution đồng thời, mỗi execution mở một kết nối DB mới, làm cạn kiệt connection limit
- giải pháp phải giải quyết đúng vấn đề cạn kiệt connection, không phải compute của Lambda hay throughput của API Gateway

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Đặt RDS Proxy giữa Lambda và RDS instance
- Duy trì một tập kết nối database đã pool sẵn (warm) mà các Lambda function chia sẻ và tái sử dụng
- Tách rời số lượng lần gọi Lambda đồng thời khỏi số lượng kết nối DB thực tế được mở
- Được AWS xây dựng chuyên biệt để giải quyết chính bài toán scaling connection giữa Lambda và RDS này

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Tăng concurrency limit của Lambda càng cho phép nhiều lần thử kết nối đồng thời hơn, làm vấn đề tệ hơn
- C — Rate limit của API Gateway kiểm soát tốc độ request API đến, không liên quan tới việc cạn kiệt connection database
- D — Tăng memory của Lambda giúp function chạy nhanh hơn nhưng không giúp giảm số lượng kết nối DB đồng thời được mở

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- "Too many connections" + Lambda + RDS gần như luôn gợi ý tới RDS Proxy
- Phân biệt các tham số scale compute (concurrency limit, memory, API rate limit) với giải pháp connection-pooling — chỉ giải pháp sau mới khắc phục được việc cạn kiệt connection DB

DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/document NoSQL store, suited to flexible document models at scale.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- key-value store for document models (composite of multiple IDs plus fields) — a NoSQL key-value/document database
- used with an ECS Fargate web tier — needs a fully managed, serverless-friendly database tier

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Launch a DynamoDB table

- Fully managed, scales automatically to match the web tier's throughput needs
- Directly matches the "key-value store" requirement stated in the scenario

- C — Amazon WorkDocs is a document collaboration/sharing tool, not a database or key-value store

- WorkDocs is a collaboration tool, never a data-tier candidate

69.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Kubernetes (EKS) is the cloud-agnostic, open-source container orchestration choice; ECS is AWS-proprietary and not portable across clouds.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- cloud-agnostic — must be portable to other cloud providers
- open-source platform — rules out AWS-proprietary services (ECS, ECR)
- same configuration/tools across environments — Kubernetes ecosystem compatibility

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Amazon EKS with EKS worker nodes
- EKS runs standard, up-to-date open-source Kubernetes, fully compatible with the broader Kubernetes ecosystem and tooling
- Applications on EKS can be migrated to Kubernetes on any other cloud or on-premises without code changes
- Satisfies both the "cloud-agnostic" and "open-source" requirements directly

- D — The same ECS proprietary-platform issue applies regardless of launch type (EC2 vs. Fargate)

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- "Cloud-agnostic" / "open-source container orchestration" points to Kubernetes/EKS, never ECS
- ECS (any launch type) is AWS-proprietary and not portable; ECR is a registry only, not an orchestrator

70.text:
CORE CONCEPT
VPC peering doesn't support edge-to-edge routing, so a second VPC's Direct Connect/VPN can't back up another VPC's connectivity; redundancy must be added directly on that VPC's own connection.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- VPC peering can't relay traffic to/from a VPC's own external connections (VPN/DX/IGW/NAT/endpoint) through the peering link to the other peer
- fault tolerance for VPC-1's on-premises connection specifically — redundancy must be added on VPC-1 itself, not via VPC-2

CORRECT ANSWER: B, E — Hardware VPN over the internet to VPC-1, and a second Direct Connect connection/private VIF in VPC-1's own region
- The edge-to-edge routing limitation means VPC-2's connections can never back up VPC-1's on-prem link
- Adding a VPN as a backup path, or an additional independent DX connection, directly to VPC-1 provides real redundancy
- Both solutions keep the redundant path attached to VPC-1 itself

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — VPN CloudHub plus a new DX/VIF built in VPC-2's region still can't be relayed to VPC-1 through peering (edge-to-edge restriction)
- C — A hardware VPN terminating at VPC-2 can't extend connectivity to VPC-1 over the peering connection
- D — A new DX connection/VIF in VPC-2's region has the same edge-to-edge limitation — it can't serve as a backup for VPC-1

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- VPC peering never supports edge-to-edge routing: a peer can't use the other peer's VPN, Direct Connect, Internet Gateway, NAT, or gateway endpoint
- Redundancy for a VPC's hybrid connection must be built directly on that VPC (e.g., a second DX connection, or VPN as backup), not through a peered VPC

CORE CONCEPT
RDS Multi-AZ automatic failover triggers only on primary-instance-affecting failures, never on standby/secondary or Read Replica issues.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- distinguish failure scenarios that affect the primary DB instance (trigger failover) from secondary/standby or Read Replica issues (do not trigger failover)

CORRECT ANSWER: A, B — Loss of availability in the primary AZ, and storage failure on the primary
- RDS automatically fails over when the primary instance itself becomes unreachable, loses network connectivity, suffers compute failure, or has storage failure
- Both listed events directly impact the primary instance, triggering automatic promotion of the standby
- The endpoint stays the same after failover, so no application reconfiguration is needed

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — Storage failure on the secondary (standby) doesn't affect the primary, so no failover occurs
- D — Read Replica failure is unrelated to the Multi-AZ standby mechanism entirely; Read Replicas don't participate in automatic failover
- E — Compute failure on the secondary instance doesn't impact the primary, so Multi-AZ failover isn't triggered

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- RDS Multi-AZ automatic failover triggers on: loss of AZ availability, network connectivity loss, compute failure, or storage failure — all specifically on the PRIMARY instance
- Read Replicas are a separate concept from the Multi-AZ standby and never trigger or participate in automatic failover

Failover tự động của RDS Multi-AZ chỉ được kích hoạt khi có sự cố ảnh hưởng tới primary instance, không bao giờ do vấn đề ở standby/secondary hay Read Replica.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- phân biệt các tình huống sự cố ảnh hưởng tới primary DB instance (kích hoạt failover) với vấn đề ở secondary/standby hay Read Replica (không kích hoạt failover)

- RDS tự động failover khi bản thân primary instance không thể truy cập được, mất kết nối mạng, gặp sự cố compute, hoặc gặp sự cố storage
- Cả hai sự kiện được liệt kê đều ảnh hưởng trực tiếp tới primary instance, kích hoạt việc promote standby tự động
- Endpoint vẫn giữ nguyên sau failover, nên không cần cấu hình lại application

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- D — Sự cố ở Read Replica hoàn toàn không liên quan tới cơ chế standby của Multi-AZ; Read Replica không tham gia vào failover tự động
- E — Sự cố compute ở secondary instance không ảnh hưởng tới primary, nên failover Multi-AZ không được kích hoạt

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Failover tự động của RDS Multi-AZ được kích hoạt khi: mất availability của AZ, mất kết nối mạng, sự cố compute, hoặc sự cố storage — tất cả đều cụ thể xảy ra ở PRIMARY instance
- Read Replica là một khái niệm tách biệt với standby của Multi-AZ và không bao giờ kích hoạt hay tham gia vào failover tự động

CORE CONCEPT
AWS Control Tower automates multi-account setup with prepackaged guardrails enforcing standardized baselines/network configs across an Organization.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- streamlined multi-account creation with preapproved configs — account factory / automated provisioning
- standardized baselines and network configs enforced per OU — guardrails (preventive/detective)
- least effort — a managed, prepackaged solution rather than custom pipelines

CORRECT ANSWER: A — AWS Control Tower Landing Zone with prepackaged guardrails
- Account Factory automates new account creation with consistent baseline configuration
- Guardrails (via SCPs, Config rules, and CloudFormation baselines) enforce or detect policy compliance automatically across OUs
- Purpose-built, lowest-effort solution for exactly this governance requirement

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- C — AWS Config aggregator plus conformance packs can standardize config monitoring but can't provision new AWS accounts at all
- D — Systems Manager OpsCenter centralizes operational issue tracking in a single account; it doesn't create accounts, and Security Hub only aggregates findings, it doesn't enforce guardrails itself

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Control Tower is the dedicated service for automated, guardrail-enforced multi-account provisioning ("Account Factory" is the key term)
- RAM (resource sharing), Config (compliance monitoring), and Security Hub (findings aggregation) each solve a narrower problem, not full account provisioning plus governance

73.text:
CORE CONCEPT
S3 Standard-IA is designed for infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond, high-throughput retrieval when requested.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- accessed less frequently, but needs rapid/immediate access when needed — defines Standard-IA exactly
- not auto-tiering (that's Intelligent-Tiering), not archival (that's Glacier)

CORRECT ANSWER: A, C — "Accessed less frequently" and "requires rapid access when needed"
- Standard-IA keeps Standard's low latency/high throughput while charging lower storage cost plus a per-GB retrieval fee
- Ideal for backups, DR data stores, and other infrequently touched but need-it-now data
- 99.999999999% durability and a 99.9% availability SLA, the same performance profile as Standard

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — Automatic movement between tiers without operational overhead describes S3 Intelligent-Tiering, not Standard-IA
- D — Standard-IA actually offers low latency and high throughput, the opposite of what this option states
- E — "Ideal for data archiving" describes S3 Glacier, not Standard-IA

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Standard-IA means infrequent access plus instant/rapid retrieval when needed, with the same performance as Standard
- Intelligent-Tiering means automatic tier movement; Glacier means archival with slower retrieval — don't mix up the three

74.text:
CORE CONCEPT
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces immutable WORM retention (even against the root user) and pairs with a lifecycle rule to archive data after the retention window.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- preserve the prior version if overwritten — versioning (implied/included with Object Lock)
- immutable for 3 years, strict regulatory compliance — Object Lock compliance mode (not governance, which allows override)
- after retention, move to archive accessed once a year — lifecycle rule to Glacier Deep Archive

CORRECT ANSWER: C — S3 Standard bucket with Object Lock in compliance mode + lifecycle rule to Glacier Deep Archive after 3 years
- Compliance mode guarantees no user, including the root account, can delete or overwrite locked objects during the retention period, satisfying strict regulatory immutability
- The lifecycle rule automatically transitions data to Glacier Deep Archive once the 3-year retention window elapses, matching the "accessed once a year" cold-access pattern
- S3 Standard provides full multi-AZ durability/availability before archival

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Versioning alone preserves prior versions but provides no immutability guarantee; without Object Lock compliance mode, objects can still be deleted/overwritten, failing regulatory compliance
- B — Governance mode permits privileged users to bypass the lock, which doesn't meet strict regulatory immutability requirements
- D — One Zone-IA lacks the multi-AZ durability/availability appropriate for critical compliance data, and this option also lacks Object Lock compliance mode

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Object Lock compliance mode means true immutability (no override, not even root); governance mode allows privileged override
- Versioning alone is not immutability — it only prevents accidental overwrite, not malicious/intentional deletion
- One Zone-IA is inappropriate for mission-critical, compliance-grade retention due to single-AZ risk

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- giữ lại version trước đó nếu bị overwrite — versioning (đi kèm/bao gồm trong Object Lock)
- bất biến trong 3 năm, tuân thủ quy định nghiêm ngặt — Object Lock compliance mode (không phải governance, vốn cho phép override)
- sau retention, chuyển sang archive được truy cập mỗi năm một lần — lifecycle rule sang Glacier Deep Archive

- Compliance mode đảm bảo không user nào, kể cả root account, có thể xóa hay overwrite object đang bị lock trong suốt retention period, đáp ứng yêu cầu bất biến theo quy định nghiêm ngặt

- S3 Standard cung cấp durability/availability multi-AZ đầy đủ trước khi archive

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- D — One Zone-IA thiếu durability/availability multi-AZ phù hợp cho dữ liệu compliance quan trọng, và phương án này cũng thiếu Object Lock compliance mode

- One Zone-IA không phù hợp cho retention mission-critical, mức độ compliance do rủi ro chỉ ở một AZ

CORE CONCEPT
Credentials for AWS API access should use IAM roles, not long-lived keys, and human console access should be hardened with MFA.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- EC2 needs access to S3/Redshift — use an IAM role attached to the instance (temporary, auto-rotated credentials)
- system administrators need secured access for deploy/test — enforce MFA on their IAM identities

CORRECT ANSWER: A, B — Enable MFA, and assign an IAM role to the EC2 instance
- IAM roles let EC2 instances make API calls using temporary, automatically rotated credentials with no hardcoded secrets
- MFA adds a second authentication factor for admins beyond username/password, securing human access
- Together these follow AWS least-privilege and credential-security best practices

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — Storing AWS Access Keys directly on the EC2 instance risks compromise if the instance is breached; IAM roles exist specifically to avoid this
- D — Assigning an IAM user per EC2 instance is unnecessary and harder to manage than a shared IAM role; roles are the correct mechanism for instance-level AWS access
- E — ACM is for provisioning/managing SSL/TLS certificates, not for storing or securing access keys

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- EC2-to-AWS-service access should use an IAM role, never hardcoded keys or per-instance IAM users
- Human account security relies on MFA; ACM is unrelated to credential storage

76.text:
CORE CONCEPT
ECS batch architectures use SQS as the inter-task message queue, with an IAM role (declared as taskRoleArn) granting ECS tasks least-privilege access to S3 and SQS.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- a queue between two ECS tasks (image upload then processing) — Amazon SQS
- IAM permissions for tasks to access S3 buckets plus the queue — an IAM role referenced via taskRoleArn in the task definition

CORRECT ANSWER: A — New SQS queue + IAM role declared as taskRoleArn in the task definition
- SQS is the standard decoupling queue for ECS batch/worker architectures, scaling automatically with incoming messages
- The second ECS task reads object names from SQS messages to retrieve and process the corresponding S3 objects
- taskRoleArn is the correct task-definition field for granting the task IAM permissions to S3 and SQS

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — AppStream 2.0 is an application streaming service, not a message queue; it can't be read from like SQS
- C — Data Firehose is for streaming delivery, not suited as a task-to-task message queue, and this option incorrectly references "taskDefinitionArn" instead of the correct "taskRoleArn" field
- D — Amazon MQ is a managed message broker, not the queue service used here; "EnableTaskIAMRole" is a legacy Windows-specific ECS setting, not the general mechanism for granting task permissions

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- SQS is the default choice for decoupling queue-based ECS task architectures
- taskRoleArn (not taskDefinitionArn) is the field that grants an ECS task its IAM permissions

CORE CONCEPT
Kiến trúc batch trên ECS dùng SQS làm message queue giữa các task, cùng một IAM role (khai báo dưới dạng taskRoleArn) cấp quyền least-privilege cho ECS task truy cập S3 và SQS.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- một queue giữa hai ECS task (upload ảnh rồi xử lý) — Amazon SQS
- permission IAM để task truy cập S3 bucket cùng với queue — một IAM role được tham chiếu qua taskRoleArn trong task definition

CORRECT ANSWER: A — SQS queue mới + IAM role được khai báo dưới dạng taskRoleArn trong task definition
- SQS là queue decoupling tiêu chuẩn cho kiến trúc batch/worker trên ECS, tự động scale theo số message đến
- ECS task thứ hai đọc tên object từ các SQS message để lấy và xử lý object S3 tương ứng
- taskRoleArn là field đúng trong task definition để cấp permission IAM cho task truy cập S3 và SQS

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- C — Data Firehose dùng cho streaming delivery, không phù hợp để làm message queue giữa các task, và phương án này còn tham chiếu sai field "taskDefinitionArn" thay vì "taskRoleArn" đúng
- D — Amazon MQ là managed message broker, không phải queue service được dùng ở đây; "EnableTaskIAMRole" là setting legacy đặc thù cho Windows trong ECS, không phải cơ chế chung để cấp permission cho task

77.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Moving a secondary Elastic Network Interface (ENI) between EC2 instances lets traffic resume on a standby instance without changing DNS or route tables.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- domain maps to the instance's private IP via its network interface — use an ENI that can be detached/reattached
- traffic must automatically resume on another instance if the primary terminates — move the ENI to the standby, preserving IP/MAC

CORRECT ANSWER: A — Secondary ENI bound to the domain's private IP, attached to the primary, moved to the standby on failure
- A secondary (non-primary) ENI can be detached and reattached to another instance, unlike an instance's primary ENI
- Moving the ENI preserves the private IP, Elastic IP, and MAC address, so traffic resumes on the new instance with no DNS/route table changes
- Directly matches the "resume traffic on another instance" requirement for a private, non-internet-facing dashboard

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — An Elastic IP is unnecessary since the application is accessed only via a private IP; AWS Transit Gateway also can't automatically reassign an EIP between instances
- C — AWS Network Firewall filters VPC-perimeter traffic; it has no ability to detach/move network interfaces
- D — AWS Transfer for FTPS is an SFTP/FTPS file transfer service, completely unrelated to detaching ENIs, and a primary ENI can't be detached in the first place

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Only a secondary ENI, never the primary one, can be detached and moved between instances
- Moving an ENI preserves private IP, EIP, and MAC, enabling failover with zero DNS/route table changes, ideal for private-subnet/internal endpoints

CORE CONCEPT
Di chuyển một Elastic Network Interface (ENI) phụ (secondary) giữa các EC2 instance cho phép traffic tiếp tục trên instance standby mà không cần đổi DNS hay route table.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- domain map tới private IP của instance thông qua network interface của nó — dùng một ENI có thể detach/reattach được
- traffic phải tự động tiếp tục trên instance khác nếu primary bị terminate — di chuyển ENI sang standby, giữ nguyên IP/MAC

CORRECT ANSWER: A — ENI phụ (secondary) gắn với private IP của domain, attach vào primary, di chuyển sang standby khi có sự cố
- Một ENI phụ (không phải ENI chính) có thể được detach và reattach sang instance khác, khác với ENI chính của instance
- Việc di chuyển ENI giữ nguyên private IP, Elastic IP, và MAC address, nên traffic tiếp tục trên instance mới mà không cần đổi DNS/route table
- Khớp trực tiếp với yêu cầu "tiếp tục traffic trên instance khác" cho một dashboard riêng tư, không hướng ra internet

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — Elastic IP không cần thiết vì application chỉ được truy cập qua private IP; AWS Transit Gateway cũng không thể tự động reassign một EIP giữa các instance
- C — AWS Network Firewall lọc traffic ở perimeter của VPC; nó không có khả năng detach/di chuyển network interface
- D — AWS Transfer for FTPS là service truyền file SFTP/FTPS, hoàn toàn không liên quan tới việc detach ENI, và ENI chính ngay từ đầu đã không thể detach được

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Chỉ ENI phụ, không bao giờ là ENI chính, mới có thể được detach và di chuyển giữa các instance
- Di chuyển một ENI giữ nguyên private IP, EIP, và MAC, cho phép failover mà không cần đổi DNS/route table, lý tưởng cho endpoint nội bộ/trong private subnet

78.text:
CORE CONCEPT
A Route 53 failover routing policy with health checks automatically redirects DNS resolution to a secondary (DR) record only when the primary is unhealthy.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- automatic routing to the DR environment only during an outage — a failover routing policy, not weighted (which always splits traffic)
- a health check on the primary endpoint to detect the outage
- the network must allow Route 53 health checker IPs through the NACL/route table
- Evaluate Target Health must be set to Yes to properly propagate health status

CORRECT ANSWER: A — Failover routing policy with a health check on the primary, NACL/route table allowing Route 53 health checks, Evaluate Target Health enabled
- Route 53 answers queries with the primary record while it's healthy, and automatically switches to the secondary (DR) record only once the primary health check fails
- Network rules must permit inbound traffic from Route 53's health-checker IP ranges for checks to succeed
- This is purpose-built for "normally primary, switch only on outage" DR patterns

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — Weighted routing distributes traffic across both primary and DR continuously by weight; it doesn't implement an outage-only switch, contradicting the "only in the event of an outage" requirement
- B — CloudWatch Alarms monitor metrics, not DNS endpoint reachability directly, and a custom Lambda plus ChangeResourceRecordSets reinvents what a native failover policy already does, with more operational overhead
- D — Same issue as B: CloudWatch Events is for AWS resource change streams, not DNS health monitoring; a native Route 53 failover configuration is the simpler, purpose-built solution

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- "Only during an outage" means a Failover routing policy, not Weighted (which always splits traffic)
- Native Route 53 health checks plus a failover policy beat custom CloudWatch+Lambda solutions for DNS-level HA
- Remember to allow Route 53 health-checker IP ranges through NACLs/route tables/firewalls

CORE CONCEPT
Routing policy failover của Route 53 kết hợp health check tự động chuyển hướng DNS resolution sang record secondary (DR) chỉ khi primary unhealthy.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- tự động routing sang môi trường DR chỉ khi có sự cố — routing policy dạng failover, không phải weighted (vốn luôn chia traffic)
- một health check trên endpoint của primary để phát hiện sự cố
- mạng phải cho phép IP của Route 53 health checker đi qua NACL/route table
- Evaluate Target Health phải được đặt là Yes để truyền đúng trạng thái health

CORRECT ANSWER: A — Routing policy failover với health check trên primary, NACL/route table cho phép health check của Route 53, bật Evaluate Target Health
- Route 53 trả lời query bằng record của primary khi nó còn healthy, và chỉ tự động chuyển sang record secondary (DR) khi health check của primary fail
- Rule mạng phải cho phép traffic inbound từ dải IP health-checker của Route 53 để health check thành công
- Đây là giải pháp được xây dựng chuyên biệt cho pattern DR "bình thường dùng primary, chỉ chuyển khi có sự cố"

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — Weighted routing phân phối traffic liên tục giữa cả primary và DR theo trọng số; nó không triển khai việc chuyển chỉ-khi-có-sự-cố, mâu thuẫn với yêu cầu "chỉ khi xảy ra sự cố"
- B — CloudWatch Alarm giám sát metric, không trực tiếp giám sát khả năng truy cập của DNS endpoint, và việc tự xây dựng Lambda cộng với ChangeResourceRecordSets chỉ làm lại những gì một failover policy có sẵn đã làm, với overhead vận hành cao hơn
- D — Cùng vấn đề như B: CloudWatch Events dùng cho stream thay đổi resource của AWS, không phải giám sát health của DNS; cấu hình failover native của Route 53 là giải pháp đơn giản hơn, được xây dựng chuyên biệt cho việc này

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- "Chỉ khi có sự cố" nghĩa là dùng routing policy Failover, không phải Weighted (vốn luôn chia traffic)
- Health check native của Route 53 cộng với failover policy tốt hơn các giải pháp CloudWatch+Lambda tự xây dựng khi nói về HA ở cấp DNS
- Nhớ cho phép dải IP health-checker của Route 53 đi qua NACL/route table/firewall

79.text:
CORE CONCEPT
IAM roles let an AWS resource (like EC2) assume permissions and obtain automatically-rotated temporary credentials, instead of embedding long-term secrets on the instance.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- EC2 needs access to S3 and other AWS services for day-to-day operations
- Credentials must be managed securely and centrally

CORRECT ANSWER: A — Create a role in IAM and assign it to the EC2 instance
- The role is attached to the instance and supplies temporary credentials via the instance metadata service
- No hardcoded/long-term credentials stored anywhere on the instance
- Centralized, auditable permission management through IAM

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — storing API credentials directly on the instance is insecure; they are exposed if the instance is compromised
- C — Security Groups control network traffic (ports/protocols), not identity or credentials; they cannot hold API keys
- D — storing credentials on a bastion host is still insecure long-term credential storage and unrelated to how EC2 itself should authenticate

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Always prefer IAM roles over embedded/hardcoded credentials for AWS resource-to-service access
- Security Groups = network-level firewall, never a credential store

KEY REQUIREMENTS

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — lưu API credentials trực tiếp trên instance là không an toàn; chúng sẽ bị lộ nếu instance bị compromise
- C — Security Groups kiểm soát network traffic (ports/protocols), không phải identity hay credentials; chúng không thể chứa API key

- Security Groups = firewall ở network level, không bao giờ là nơi lưu credential

80.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Amazon GuardDuty is a managed threat-detection service that uses anomaly detection, machine learning, and threat intelligence to flag malicious or suspicious activity, including on S3.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Encrypted documents continually sent to S3 — compliance-grade access configuration needed
- Must alert on unauthorized access or suspicious access patterns, not just log them

CORRECT ANSWER: A — Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor malicious activity on S3
- Detects findings such as requests from known-malicious IPs, bucket policy/ACL changes that expose a bucket publicly, and suspicious API call patterns
- Combines anomaly detection, ML, and continuously updated threat intel to proactively alert

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — AWS CloudTrail records API calls for governance/compliance/audit purposes; it logs activity but is not itself a threat-detection/alerting engine for suspicious S3 access patterns
- C — Amazon Rekognition analyzes images/video (objects, people, inappropriate content); unrelated to access-pattern monitoring
- D — Amazon Inspector is an automated security assessment service for workloads (e.g., EC2, container images), not an S3 access-monitoring/alerting tool

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- GuardDuty = continuous threat detection/alerting across account activity, including S3 protection
- CloudTrail = audit log of API activity; pairs with GuardDuty but doesn't replace it for anomaly alerting

- Kết hợp anomaly detection, ML và threat intel luôn được cập nhật để chủ động cảnh báo

81.text:
CORE CONCEPT
A CDN (CloudFront) paired with durable object storage (S3) is the standard, cost-effective way to globally distribute static content with low latency.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Static content delivered globally to premium users and partners
- Must reduce server costs and deliver securely with low latency

CORRECT ANSWER: A, D — Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
- S3 stores static files durably and cheaply; no servers to manage or scale
- CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide for low-latency delivery
- CloudFront integrates natively with S3 as an origin, with AWS Shield for DDoS protection, and no data transfer charges between S3/EC2/ELB and CloudFront
- Flow: Client -> CloudFront edge (cache) -> S3 origin (on cache miss)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers; costs more than S3 for storing static content and adds unnecessary compute
- C — AWS Lambda runs code serverlessly but cannot store static content or act as a CDN
- E — AWS Global Accelerator suits non-HTTP/UDP use cases (gaming, IoT, VoIP) or static-IP/fast-failover HTTP needs; it does not integrate directly with S3 for static content delivery

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Default pairing for global static content delivery: S3 (storage) + CloudFront (CDN)
- Global Accelerator vs CloudFront: Accelerator optimizes TCP/UDP routing to regions; CloudFront caches content at edge

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Nội dung static được phân phối toàn cầu cho premium user và partner
- Phải giảm chi phí server và phân phối an toàn với latency thấp

CORRECT ANSWER: A, D — Amazon CloudFront và Amazon S3
- S3 lưu trữ file static một cách bền vững và rẻ; không cần quản lý hay scale server nào
- CloudFront cache nội dung tại các edge location trên toàn thế giới để phân phối với latency thấp
- CloudFront tích hợp native với S3 như một origin, có AWS Shield bảo vệ DDoS, và không tính phí data transfer giữa S3/EC2/ELB và CloudFront
- Luồng: Client -> CloudFront edge (cache) -> S3 origin (khi cache miss)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — AWS Fargate là serverless compute engine cho container; tốn chi phí hơn S3 để lưu nội dung static và thêm compute không cần thiết
- C — AWS Lambda chạy code theo kiểu serverless nhưng không thể lưu nội dung static hay đóng vai trò CDN
- E — AWS Global Accelerator phù hợp cho use case non-HTTP/UDP (gaming, IoT, VoIP) hoặc nhu cầu static-IP/fast-failover cho HTTP; nó không tích hợp trực tiếp với S3 để phân phối nội dung static

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Cặp mặc định để phân phối nội dung static toàn cầu: S3 (storage) + CloudFront (CDN)
- Global Accelerator vs CloudFront: Accelerator tối ưu routing TCP/UDP đến các region; CloudFront cache nội dung tại edge

82.text:
CORE CONCEPT
SQS queues cannot prioritize individual messages, so differentiated service levels require separate queues per priority tier, consumed in priority order.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Premium members must be processed with higher priority than free members
- All requests currently share a single SQS queue feeding EC2 consumers

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Separate SQS queues for free and premium members; consume premium first, then free
- EC2 instances poll the premium queue first; only poll the free-members queue when the premium queue is empty
- Achieves effective prioritization using standard SQS semantics (no native per-message priority exists)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — SQS has no concept of per-message priority within a single queue; cannot be configured this way
- C — Kinesis is for real-time streaming data ingestion/processing, not applicable to this queue-priority problem
- D — S3 is durable storage, not a processing/queuing mechanism; doesn't address prioritization

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- SQS messages within one queue have no priority ordering — use multiple queues to simulate priority tiers
- Pattern: poll high-priority queue first, fall back to lower-priority queue when empty

CORE CONCEPT
SQS queue không thể ưu tiên từng message riêng lẻ, nên để có các mức độ service khác nhau cần tách thành các queue riêng theo từng tier ưu tiên, và consume theo thứ tự ưu tiên.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Premium member phải được xử lý với độ ưu tiên cao hơn free member
- Hiện tất cả request đang dùng chung một SQS queue, được EC2 consumer xử lý

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Tách SQS queue riêng cho free và premium member; consume premium trước, sau đó mới đến free
- EC2 instance poll queue premium trước; chỉ poll queue free-members khi queue premium đã rỗng
- Đạt được việc ưu tiên hiệu quả bằng cách dùng semantics chuẩn của SQS (không có khái niệm per-message priority gốc)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — SQS không có khái niệm priority cho từng message trong một queue; không thể cấu hình theo cách này
- C — Kinesis dùng cho real-time streaming data ingestion/processing, không áp dụng cho bài toán ưu tiên queue này
- D — S3 là durable storage, không phải cơ chế processing/queuing; không giải quyết được vấn đề ưu tiên

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Message trong một SQS queue không có thứ tự ưu tiên — dùng nhiều queue để giả lập các tier ưu tiên
- Pattern: poll queue ưu tiên cao trước, fallback sang queue ưu tiên thấp hơn khi rỗng

83.text:
CORE CONCEPT
S3 Object Lock (WORM) combined with lifecycle transitions to Glacier Deep Archive satisfies both "preserve prior versions" and "long-term compliance archival" requirements.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Previous file state must be preserved/retrievable after modification — needs versioning/Object Lock
- Data over 3 years must move to archive storage, accessed only ~once/year
- Must meet regulatory compliance — requires guaranteed immutability, not just optional protection

CORRECT ANSWER: C — S3 Standard with Object Lock in Compliance mode + lifecycle rule to Glacier Deep Archive after 3 years
- Compliance mode prevents any user — including the root account — from overwriting or deleting an object version for the retention period, satisfying strict regulatory compliance
- Lifecycle rule automatically transitions data older than 3 years to Glacier Deep Archive, the cheapest long-term archive tier suited to ~annual access

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — plain versioning without Object Lock in compliance mode does not guarantee immutability, so it fails the strict regulatory requirement
- B — Governance mode allows certain privileged users to remove the lock, so it doesn't meet strict compliance needs
- D — One Zone-IA lacks the multi-AZ durability/availability appropriate for compliance-critical data, and it still lacks Object Lock compliance mode

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Object Lock Compliance mode = nobody (incl. root) can delete/overwrite during retention; Governance mode = privileged users can override
- Lifecycle rules to Glacier Deep Archive are the standard pattern for rarely-accessed, long-retention compliance data

CORE CONCEPT
S3 Object Lock (WORM) kết hợp với lifecycle transition sang Glacier Deep Archive đáp ứng cả yêu cầu "giữ lại trạng thái file trước đó" lẫn "archival lưu trữ dài hạn cho compliance".

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Trạng thái file trước đó phải được giữ lại/truy xuất được sau khi chỉnh sửa — cần versioning/Object Lock
- Dữ liệu trên 3 năm phải chuyển sang archive storage, chỉ truy cập khoảng 1 lần/năm
- Phải đáp ứng compliance quy định — cần tính immutability được đảm bảo, không chỉ là bảo vệ tùy chọn

CORRECT ANSWER: C — S3 Standard với Object Lock ở Compliance mode + lifecycle rule chuyển sang Glacier Deep Archive sau 3 năm
- Compliance mode ngăn bất kỳ user nào — kể cả root account — ghi đè hoặc xóa một object version trong thời gian retention, đáp ứng yêu cầu compliance quy định nghiêm ngặt
- Lifecycle rule tự động chuyển dữ liệu cũ hơn 3 năm sang Glacier Deep Archive, tier archive dài hạn rẻ nhất phù hợp với tần suất truy cập ~hàng năm

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — chỉ dùng versioning thông thường mà không có Object Lock compliance mode thì không đảm bảo được immutability, nên không đáp ứng yêu cầu compliance nghiêm ngặt
- B — Governance mode cho phép một số privileged user gỡ bỏ lock, nên không đáp ứng được nhu cầu compliance nghiêm ngặt
- D — One Zone-IA thiếu durability/availability multi-AZ phù hợp cho dữ liệu compliance-critical, và vẫn thiếu Object Lock compliance mode

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Object Lock Compliance mode = không ai (kể cả root) có thể xóa/ghi đè trong thời gian retention; Governance mode = privileged user có thể override
- Lifecycle rule sang Glacier Deep Archive là pattern chuẩn cho dữ liệu compliance ít truy cập, retention dài

84.text:
CORE CONCEPT
A DynamoDB Gateway VPC endpoint keeps DynamoDB traffic off the public internet, while AWS Backup (not native on-demand backups) is required for cross-account/cross-region backup copies.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Database calls must not traverse the public internet — needs a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB
- Automated cross-account backup for long-term retention — native DynamoDB on-demand backups cannot be copied across accounts/regions

CORRECT ANSWER: A — DynamoDB gateway endpoint associated to the route table + AWS Backup to copy on-demand backups to another account
- Gateway endpoint updates the route table with a DynamoDB prefix list as destination and the endpoint as target, keeping traffic within the AWS network via private IPs
- AWS Backup supports copying backups across accounts/regions, adding cost allocation tags, and transitioning to cold storage — native on-demand DynamoDB backups alone cannot do this

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — DynamoDB only supports Gateway endpoints, not Interface endpoints; also PITR only restores within the same account/region, no cross-account support
- C — NACL rules alone don't guarantee traffic stays off the public internet, and native on-demand backups still can't be copied cross-account
- D — DynamoDB doesn't support Interface endpoints; Network Firewall integrates with VPCs, not individual service endpoints directly in this way; Amazon Timestream is an unrelated time-series DB and cannot provide DynamoDB PITR

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- DynamoDB VPC endpoints are Gateway type only (like S3), not Interface type
- Native on-demand DynamoDB backups: single account/region only; cross-account/region backup requires AWS Backup
- PITR restores within the same account/region; it does not enable cross-account recovery

CORE CONCEPT

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Database call không được đi qua public internet — cần VPC endpoint cho DynamoDB
- Backup tự động cross-account cho retention dài hạn — native on-demand backup của DynamoDB không thể copy qua account/region khác

CORRECT ANSWER: A — DynamoDB gateway endpoint gắn vào route table + AWS Backup để copy on-demand backup sang account khác
- Gateway endpoint cập nhật route table với một prefix list của DynamoDB làm destination và endpoint làm target, giữ traffic trong mạng AWS qua private IP
- AWS Backup hỗ trợ copy backup qua account/region khác, thêm cost allocation tag, và chuyển sang cold storage — native on-demand DynamoDB backup đơn thuần không làm được điều này

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — DynamoDB chỉ hỗ trợ Gateway endpoint, không hỗ trợ Interface endpoint; ngoài ra PITR chỉ restore trong cùng account/region, không hỗ trợ cross-account
- C — chỉ dùng NACL rule không đảm bảo traffic sẽ không đi qua public internet, và native on-demand backup vẫn không thể copy cross-account
- D — DynamoDB không hỗ trợ Interface endpoint; Network Firewall tích hợp với VPC, không trực tiếp với từng service endpoint theo cách này; Amazon Timestream là time-series DB không liên quan và không thể cung cấp PITR cho DynamoDB

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- DynamoDB VPC endpoint chỉ có loại Gateway (giống S3), không có loại Interface
- Native on-demand DynamoDB backup: chỉ trong cùng account/region; backup cross-account/region cần AWS Backup
- PITR chỉ restore trong cùng account/region; không hỗ trợ recovery cross-account

85.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Communication between EC2 instances in different subnets of the same VPC depends on Network ACLs (subnet-level, stateless) and Security Groups (instance-level, stateful) both permitting the traffic.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Two instances in different subnets, same AZ, need to communicate for app-to-database connectivity
- Must verify both the subnet-level and instance-level traffic controls

CORRECT ANSWER: A, D — Check NACLs allow communication between the subnets; check Security Groups allow the app host to reach the database on the correct port/protocol
- NACLs act as a stateless firewall between subnets and must explicitly allow the traffic in both directions
- Security Groups must allow inbound traffic on the DB's port/protocol from the application instance (or its SG)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — instance class/type has no bearing on network connectivity between instances
- C — a NAT instance/Internet Gateway is only needed for internet-bound traffic, not for intra-VPC communication
- E — Placement Groups provide low-latency, high-throughput networking for tightly-coupled workloads; they are not required for basic connectivity

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Intra-VPC connectivity troubleshooting checklist: NACL (stateless, subnet-level) + Security Group (stateful, instance-level)
- IGW/NAT only matter for traffic to/from the internet, not VPC-internal traffic

Giao tiếp giữa các EC2 instance ở các subnet khác nhau trong cùng VPC phụ thuộc vào Network ACL (cấp subnet, stateless) và Security Group (cấp instance, stateful) đều phải cho phép traffic đó.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Hai instance ở subnet khác nhau, cùng AZ, cần giao tiếp để app kết nối tới database
- Phải kiểm tra cả traffic control ở cấp subnet lẫn cấp instance

CORRECT ANSWER: A, D — Kiểm tra NACL cho phép giao tiếp giữa các subnet; kiểm tra Security Group cho phép app host kết nối tới database đúng port/protocol
- NACL hoạt động như firewall stateless giữa các subnet và phải cho phép traffic đó rõ ràng theo cả hai chiều
- Security Group phải cho phép traffic inbound trên port/protocol của DB từ application instance (hoặc SG của nó)

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — instance class/type không ảnh hưởng đến khả năng kết nối network giữa các instance
- C — NAT instance/Internet Gateway chỉ cần thiết cho traffic đi ra internet, không cần cho giao tiếp nội bộ trong VPC
- E — Placement Group cung cấp networking latency thấp, throughput cao cho workload tightly-coupled; không bắt buộc cho kết nối cơ bản

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Checklist troubleshoot kết nối nội bộ VPC: NACL (stateless, cấp subnet) + Security Group (stateful, cấp instance)
- IGW/NAT chỉ liên quan đến traffic đi đến/từ internet, không liên quan traffic nội bộ VPC

86.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's global edge network to speed up uploads/downloads to/from a single S3 bucket over long distances, without needing extra infrastructure.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Outposts servers worldwide repeatedly download multi-file software updates from a single us-west-2 bucket
- Must minimize deployment latency AND minimize operational overhead

CORRECT ANSWER: C — Use S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing bucket; Outposts servers use the acceleration endpoint
- Requires no new distributions, origins, or signed-URL infrastructure — just point downloads at the acceleration endpoint
- Leverages AWS's global network backbone to reduce latency for geographically distant Outposts servers with minimal setup

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — a secondary origin with a CachingDisabled policy defeats the purpose of caching, which is key to reducing latency for repeated large-file downloads
- B — Global Accelerator improves general app availability/performance via routing, but doesn't integrate directly with S3 downloads; private VIF is a Direct Connect concept, not applicable here
- D — a single-origin CloudFront distribution with signed URLs adds management overhead (distribution + signed URL infrastructure) compared to simply enabling Transfer Acceleration on the existing bucket

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- S3 Transfer Acceleration: least-effort speed boost for existing bucket, best for widely distributed clients accessing one bucket
- CloudFront: better when you need caching of frequently-requested, cacheable content across many requesters; added setup overhead

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Các Outposts server trên toàn thế giới liên tục tải về các bản cập nhật phần mềm nhiều file từ một bucket duy nhất ở us-west-2
- Phải giảm thiểu latency khi triển khai VÀ giảm thiểu operational overhead

CORRECT ANSWER: C — Dùng S3 Transfer Acceleration trên bucket hiện có; Outposts server dùng acceleration endpoint
- Không cần distribution mới, origin mới, hay hạ tầng signed-URL — chỉ cần trỏ download tới acceleration endpoint
- Tận dụng global network backbone của AWS để giảm latency cho các Outposts server ở xa về địa lý với thiết lập tối thiểu

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- B — Global Accelerator cải thiện availability/performance tổng thể của app thông qua routing, nhưng không tích hợp trực tiếp với download từ S3; private VIF là khái niệm của Direct Connect, không áp dụng ở đây
- D — một CloudFront distribution single-origin với signed URL làm tăng overhead quản lý (distribution + hạ tầng signed URL) so với việc chỉ đơn giản bật Transfer Acceleration trên bucket hiện có

EXAM TAKEAWAY

- CloudFront: tốt hơn khi cần cache nội dung được yêu cầu thường xuyên, có thể cache được, bởi nhiều requester khác nhau; thêm overhead thiết lập

87.text:
CORE CONCEPT
AWS Snowball is a petabyte-scale offline data transport appliance ideal when available internet bandwidth would make an online transfer take too long.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- 250 TB of archive data to migrate to S3
- Only a 100 Mbps dedicated line is available — must be the fastest AND most cost-effective method

CORRECT ANSWER: D — Order multiple AWS Snowball devices to upload the files to S3
- Rule of thumb: if transfer over existing bandwidth would take more than ~1 week, use Snowball instead
- At 100 Mbps, 250 TB would take months online; multiple Snowballs complete the transfer in about a week, at a fraction of the cost of upgrading network infrastructure

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — direct upload over the 100 Mbps line would take far too long given the data volume
- B — Direct Connect takes time to provision and is meant for ongoing dedicated connectivity, not optimal for a one-time 250 TB migration
- C — Snowmobile is built for exabyte-scale transfers (up to 100 PB) via a 45-foot truck-trailer; massive overkill and not cost-effective for only 250 TB

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Decision rule: if transfer time over existing link > ~1 week, use Snowball/Snowball Edge/Snowmobile instead of network transfer
- Snowmobile is for exabyte-scale (up to 100PB); Snowball/Snowball Edge for typical large (TB-PB) one-time migrations

KEY REQUIREMENTS

- Chỉ có một đường dây dedicated 100 Mbps — phải là phương pháp nhanh nhất VÀ tiết kiệm chi phí nhất

CORRECT ANSWER: D — Đặt nhiều thiết bị AWS Snowball để upload file lên S3

- Ở tốc độ 100 Mbps, 250 TB sẽ mất vài tháng nếu transfer online; nhiều Snowball hoàn thành việc transfer trong khoảng một tuần, với chi phí chỉ bằng một phần nhỏ so với việc nâng cấp hạ tầng mạng

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT

- C — Snowmobile được thiết kế cho transfer quy mô exabyte (lên đến 100 PB) qua một xe container dài 45 feet; quá dư thừa và không tiết kiệm chi phí cho chỉ 250 TB

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Quy tắc quyết định: nếu thời gian transfer qua đường link hiện có > ~1 tuần, dùng Snowball/Snowball Edge/Snowmobile thay vì transfer qua mạng
- Snowmobile dành cho quy mô exabyte (lên đến 100PB); Snowball/Snowball Edge dành cho migrate quy mô lớn thông thường (TB-PB) một lần

88.text:
CORE CONCEPT
EBS volumes are durable, off-instance block storage that persists independently of instance lifecycle and support live, in-place configuration changes.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Must address compliance, downtime, and IOPS performance concerns about EBS
- Need factually accurate EBS characteristics to justify its use for migration

CORRECT ANSWER: C, D — EBS is off-instance storage that persists independently of the instance's life; and EBS supports live configuration changes (volume type, size, IOPS) without service interruption
- Off-instance persistence means data survives instance termination if configured, proving durability
- Live modification of type/size/IOPS addresses the performance-tuning and no-downtime concern directly

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — EBS volumes are replicated within the same Availability Zone only, not across regions
- B — an EBS volume can only attach to an EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone, not any AZ
- E — EBS snapshots are written to Amazon S3 (redundantly across AZs), not to Amazon RDS

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- EBS replication is intra-AZ, not cross-region; volumes attach only within the same AZ
- EBS snapshots live in S3; EBS supports live volume modification (type/size/IOPS) without downtime

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Phải giải quyết các lo ngại về compliance, downtime, và hiệu năng IOPS của EBS
- Cần các phát biểu chính xác về đặc điểm của EBS để biện minh cho việc dùng nó trong migration

CORRECT ANSWER: C, D — EBS là storage nằm ngoài instance, tồn tại độc lập với vòng đời của instance; và EBS hỗ trợ thay đổi cấu hình trực tiếp (volume type, size, IOPS) mà không gián đoạn dịch vụ
- Tính bền vững nằm ngoài instance nghĩa là dữ liệu vẫn tồn tại sau khi instance bị terminate nếu được cấu hình đúng, chứng minh được độ durable
- Việc thay đổi type/size/IOPS trực tiếp giải quyết trực tiếp mối lo về tinh chỉnh hiệu năng và không downtime

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — EBS volume chỉ được replicate trong cùng một Availability Zone, không phải across region
- B — một EBS volume chỉ có thể attach vào EC2 instance trong cùng Availability Zone, không phải bất kỳ AZ nào
- E — EBS snapshot được ghi vào Amazon S3 (được replicate dư thừa across AZ), không phải vào Amazon RDS

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- EBS replication chỉ trong cùng AZ, không phải cross-region; volume chỉ attach được trong cùng AZ
- EBS snapshot nằm trên S3; EBS hỗ trợ thay đổi volume trực tiếp (type/size/IOPS) mà không downtime

89.text:
CORE CONCEPT
CloudWatch provides metric monitoring/alarming, and SNS delivers the resulting notifications (including email) — the standard pairing for "monitor + alert" requirements.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Monitor specific database metrics
- Send email notifications to Operations when issues occur

CORRECT ANSWER: B, E — Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon SNS
- CloudWatch collects metrics/logs/events and triggers alarms on threshold breaches
- SNS is the pub/sub messaging service used to fan out notifications (including email) triggered by CloudWatch alarms

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Amazon SES is designed for sending bulk/transactional/marketing email, not for system/monitoring notifications; SNS is the correct choice for alerting
- C — SQS is a message queuing service; it doesn't monitor metrics or send notifications
- D — a BIND server on EC2 is a DNS service, unrelated to monitoring or notifications

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Standard alerting pattern: CloudWatch (detect/alarm) + SNS (notify)
- SES = bulk/transactional email sending; SNS = system/application notifications and pub/sub messaging — don't confuse the two

CloudWatch cung cấp giám sát metric/alarm, và SNS gửi các thông báo kết quả (bao gồm cả email) — đây là cặp chuẩn cho yêu cầu "giám sát + cảnh báo".

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Giám sát các metric database cụ thể
- Gửi thông báo email cho bộ phận Operations khi có vấn đề xảy ra

CORRECT ANSWER: B, E — Amazon CloudWatch và Amazon SNS
- CloudWatch thu thập metric/log/event và kích hoạt alarm khi vượt ngưỡng
- SNS là dịch vụ messaging pub/sub dùng để fan-out thông báo (bao gồm email) được kích hoạt bởi CloudWatch alarm

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Amazon SES được thiết kế để gửi email hàng loạt/giao dịch/marketing, không phải cho thông báo system/monitoring; SNS mới là lựa chọn đúng cho việc cảnh báo
- C — SQS là dịch vụ message queuing; nó không giám sát metric hay gửi thông báo
- D — một BIND server trên EC2 là dịch vụ DNS, không liên quan đến monitoring hay notification

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Pattern cảnh báo chuẩn: CloudWatch (phát hiện/alarm) + SNS (thông báo)
- SES = gửi email hàng loạt/giao dịch; SNS = thông báo system/application và messaging pub/sub — đừng nhầm lẫn hai cái này

90.text:
CORE CONCEPT
API Gateway is a fully managed service for building RESTful and WebSocket APIs optimized for serverless backends, billed purely on usage (API calls + data transfer).

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Need to describe API Gateway's actual capabilities across multiple client platforms
- Must distinguish real features from capabilities of other AWS services

CORRECT ANSWER: C, E — Enables building RESTful and WebSocket APIs optimized for serverless workloads; pay only for API calls received and data transferred out
- Acts as a managed "front door" to backend compute (Lambda, EC2, or any web app) with no servers to manage for the API layer itself
- No minimum fees/startup costs — pure usage-based pricing

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — API Gateway does not auto-provide a GraphQL-like query language; that's not a built-in feature
- B — static anycast IP addresses as a fixed entry point is a feature of AWS Global Accelerator, not API Gateway
- D — custom OS-bypass hardware interface for high inter-node communication describes Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), not API Gateway

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- API Gateway = managed REST/WebSocket API front door, pay-per-call pricing, pairs naturally with Lambda
- Don't confuse with Global Accelerator (static anycast IPs) or EFA (low-latency inter-node HPC networking)

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Cần mô tả đúng khả năng thực tế của API Gateway trên nhiều nền tảng client
- Phải phân biệt tính năng thật với khả năng của các AWS service khác

CORRECT ANSWER: C, E — Cho phép xây dựng RESTful và WebSocket API được tối ưu cho serverless workload; chỉ trả tiền cho số API call nhận được và data transferred out
- Đóng vai trò như một "cửa trước" managed tới backend compute (Lambda, EC2, hay bất kỳ web app nào) mà không cần quản lý server nào cho tầng API
- Không có phí tối thiểu/chi phí khởi tạo — tính phí hoàn toàn theo usage

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — API Gateway không tự động cung cấp một query language kiểu GraphQL; đó không phải tính năng built-in
- B — static anycast IP address như một entry point cố định là tính năng của AWS Global Accelerator, không phải API Gateway
- D — custom OS-bypass hardware interface cho giao tiếp inter-node tốc độ cao mô tả Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), không phải API Gateway

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- API Gateway = managed REST/WebSocket API front door, pricing theo pay-per-call, kết hợp tự nhiên với Lambda
- Đừng nhầm với Global Accelerator (static anycast IP) hay EFA (HPC networking inter-node latency thấp)

91.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Lambda@Edge runs custom code at CloudFront edge locations, allowing per-request logic such as serving different content formats and modifying response headers, all with minimal operational overhead.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Serve WebP to supporting user agents, JPEG otherwise — content negotiation based on User-Agent
- Add a custom tracking header to the response
- Minimize operational overhead (no extra servers/distributions)

CORRECT ANSWER: A — CloudFront behaviors plus Lambda@Edge functions to inspect User-Agent, serve the right format, and modify response headers
- Lambda@Edge intercepts the viewer request/response at the edge, enabling dynamic format selection and header injection in one integrated mechanism
- No additional servers, distributions, or services required

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- B — running multiple distributions per format plus Route 53-based routing on User-Agent adds unnecessary complexity and operational overhead
- C — a CloudFront response headers policy only controls which headers are included/excluded; it cannot dynamically select image format based on User-Agent
- D — building a custom EC2-based image conversion service adds significant operational burden versus the built-in Lambda@Edge approach

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Lambda@Edge = run code at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests/responses (format negotiation, header manipulation, personalization)
- Response headers policies only add/remove/override headers — they contain no conditional logic

- Lambda@Edge can thiệp vào viewer request/response tại edge, cho phép chọn định dạng động và inject header trong một cơ chế tích hợp duy nhất
- Không cần thêm server, distribution, hay service nào khác

- Response headers policy chỉ thêm/xóa/override header — không chứa logic điều kiện nào

92.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Routing a custom domain via Route 53 to an S3 static website requires an exact bucket-name-to-domain match and a registered domain name — Route 53 itself does not require same-region placement or CORS for basic routing.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- S3 bucket configured for static website hosting, name must exactly match the domain/subdomain
- A registered domain name (via Route 53 or another registrar), with Route 53 as the DNS service

CORRECT ANSWER: A, B — The S3 bucket name must match the domain name; a registered domain name is required
- Route 53 maps the domain to the S3 website endpoint; the bucket name requirement lets Route 53's alias record resolve to the correct website endpoint
- A domain must already be registered (through Route 53 or elsewhere) before routing can be configured

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — an MX record is for mail server resolution, unrelated to routing web traffic to S3
- D — there is no requirement that the S3 bucket be in the same region as the Route 53 hosted zone
- E — CORS is only needed when a web app on one domain needs to call resources on a different domain; not a prerequisite for basic Route 53-to-S3 routing

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- S3 static website + Route 53: bucket name MUST equal the domain/subdomain name — this is the most commonly tested gotcha
- No region-matching or CORS requirement exists just for routing traffic to an S3 website endpoint

Định tuyến một domain tùy chỉnh qua Route 53 tới S3 static website yêu cầu tên bucket phải khớp chính xác với domain và một domain name đã được đăng ký — bản thân Route 53 không yêu cầu cùng region hay CORS cho việc định tuyến cơ bản.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- S3 bucket được cấu hình để static website hosting, tên phải khớp chính xác với domain/subdomain
- Một domain name đã đăng ký (qua Route 53 hoặc registrar khác), với Route 53 là DNS service

CORRECT ANSWER: A, B — Tên S3 bucket phải khớp với domain name; cần một domain name đã đăng ký
- Route 53 ánh xạ domain tới S3 website endpoint; yêu cầu tên bucket cho phép alias record của Route 53 resolve đến đúng website endpoint
- Một domain phải được đăng ký trước (qua Route 53 hoặc nơi khác) trước khi có thể cấu hình routing

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- C — MX record dùng để resolve mail server, không liên quan đến việc route web traffic tới S3
- D — không có yêu cầu nào bắt S3 bucket phải cùng region với Route 53 hosted zone
- E — CORS chỉ cần thiết khi một web app ở một domain cần gọi resource ở domain khác; không phải điều kiện tiên quyết cho việc định tuyến cơ bản từ Route 53 tới S3

93.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Decoupled architectures connecting on-premises and cloud components rely on messaging/workflow services (SQS, SWF) to pass work between independently-scaling components, not databases or direct network peering.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Resources span AWS and on-premises servers
- Architecture must be decoupled (components operate independently while interfacing with each other)

CORRECT ANSWER: A, C — Use SWF and SQS to decouple on-premises servers and EC2 instances
- SQS: reliable, highly scalable managed queues for passing messages between distributed components, enabling decoupling
- SWF: coordinates distributed work/tasks across components, also supporting decoupled designs

- E — DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service, also not a decoupling mechanism
- D — VPC peering cannot connect an on-premises network to a VPC; peering is VPC-to-VPC only (use VPN/Direct Connect for on-premises connectivity)

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Decoupling building blocks: SQS (queuing) and SWF/Step Functions (workflow orchestration) — not databases
- VPC Peering only connects VPCs to each other, never on-premises networks directly

96.text:
CORE CONCEPT
Route 53 DNS failover can redirect traffic to a static S3-hosted website or CloudFront distribution when the primary application becomes unavailable, without duplicating the full architecture.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Anticipate high traffic and potential load failure for a new MEAN stack web app
- Need an automatic DNS-level failover to a simple, reliable static fallback

CORRECT ANSWER: C — Use Route 53 with the failover routing option pointed at a static S3 website bucket or CloudFront distribution
- Route 53 health checks detect the primary endpoint's failure and automatically shift DNS resolution to the static fallback target
- Avoids the cost and complexity of a fully duplicated live environment

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — duplicating the full application stack in another region with weighted routing is a distributed active-active setup, not a cost-effective failover mechanism, and doesn't match the ask
- B — failing over to an on-premises data center works but doesn't leverage Route 53's native failover capability within AWS
- D — simply adding more servers after failure still leaves a downtime gap while new servers spin up; it's reactive, not a failover design

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Route 53 failover routing policy + health checks is the standard lightweight DR pattern, often paired with a static S3/CloudFront "sorry page" or minimal fallback site
- Failover ≠ scaling — failover is about rerouting during an outage, not adding capacity

- Cần failover tự động ở cấp DNS sang một fallback static đơn giản, đáng tin cậy

- Tránh được chi phí và độ phức tạp của việc nhân bản toàn bộ một môi trường live

- B — failover sang một data center on-premises vẫn hoạt động nhưng không tận dụng được khả năng failover native của Route 53 trong AWS

AWS Snowball Edge adds on-board compute/storage to the standard Snowball offline-transfer appliance, making it the cost-effective choice for large (but not exabyte-scale) one-time data migrations under tight bandwidth.

- 80 TB data warehouse migration that would take 2 months over current bandwidth
- Needs the most cost-effective way to upload quickly

CORRECT ANSWER: B — AWS Snowball Edge
- Physically ships data via regional carrier at speeds faster than available internet bandwidth allows
- Available in storage-optimized, compute-optimized, and GPU configurations; appropriately sized for tens of TB like this 80 TB scenario

- Direct Connect is for ongoing connectivity, not one-off bulk migrations

CORE CONCEPT
AWS STS issues short-lived temporary security credentials (via AssumeRole) that let a trusted identity in one account access resources in another account under a defined role.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Developer needs temporary, short-lived access to the production account
- Access must be scoped to write-only on EC2 and S3

CORRECT ANSWER: B — Use AWS Security Token Service (STS)
- The developer (in the Dev account) calls AssumeRole on an IAM role (e.g., WriteAccess) defined in the Prod account
- STS returns temporary credentials scoped to that role's permissions, usable to call S3/EC2 APIs in Prod, and these expire automatically
- Flow: Dev account user -> AssumeRole (STS) -> temporary credentials -> access scoped resources in Prod account

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — Amazon Cognito/JWT is for application user authentication and session management, not for granting temporary AWS resource access across accounts
- C — AWS IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access management across accounts/apps, but it is not the mechanism that issues short-lived AssumeRole-style tokens for this cross-account resource access pattern
- D — "All of the above" is wrong since only STS provides the described temporary credential mechanism

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Cross-account temporary access = STS AssumeRole, producing time-limited credentials
- Cognito = app user identity/session tokens; IAM Identity Center = workforce SSO portal access, not raw temporary AWS API credentials

Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) automates the full lifecycle (creation, retention, deletion) of EBS snapshots at no extra cost, making it the fastest built-in way to implement automated backups.

- Must be implemented fast and cost-effectively

- Works alongside CloudWatch Events/CloudTrail for monitoring, at no additional service cost

100.text:
CORE CONCEPT
The Auto Scaling cooldown period is a configurable pause after a scaling activity that prevents the group from launching/terminating more instances before the previous action's effects are fully realized.

KEY REQUIREMENTS
- Protect against unintended slowdown/unavailability from scaling too aggressively
- Need factually accurate statements about cooldown behavior, including its default value

CORRECT ANSWER: C, D — Cooldown ensures the Auto Scaling group doesn't launch/terminate additional instances before the previous scaling activity takes effect; its default value is 300 seconds
- After a simple scaling policy triggers a scale event, the ASG pauses for the cooldown duration before evaluating further scaling actions
- Default cooldown is 300 seconds, and it is a configurable setting per Auto Scaling group

WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE INCORRECT
- A — cooldown is not about scale-out instances "warming up" before launch; that's a different concept (e.g., warm-up/health-check grace period)
- B — cooldown does not guarantee zero downtime during launch/terminate events; it only paces subsequent scaling actions
- E — the default cooldown value is 300 seconds, not 600 seconds

EXAM TAKEAWAY
- Cooldown default = 300 seconds; it paces consecutive scaling activities, it does not eliminate downtime or describe instance warm-up
- Don't confuse cooldown with ASG health check grace period or instance warm-up time for scaling metrics

- Sau khi một simple scaling policy kích hoạt một scale event, ASG tạm dừng trong khoảng thời gian cooldown trước khi đánh giá thêm hành động scaling nào khác
